statusText: NQ futures remain in the CME Friday-evening weekend halt, roughly an hour past the prior run and still well ahead of Sunday's reopen, leaving no live price path to evaluate. Since the prior run (22:27 UTC), no material developments have emerged: the Strait of Hormuz crisis holds at its previously confirmed state -- the Thursday-evening two-tanker ADNOC drone attack plus the separate drone strike on an exiting tanker remain the latest confirmed incidents, with WebSearch this hour surfacing only recap/live-blog coverage of the same episode and no new discrete escalation. VIX's last confirmed print remains the calm Friday close near 14.6; the 10-year Treasury yield's last confirmed level remains near 4.7%, both carried forward from the prior run since no live U.S. session is open to re-verify them. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota is again exhausted this run (MARKET_STATUS call returned a rate_limit error), so this run relies entirely on WebSearch corroboration of already-known facts; Confidence stays low given the continued Alpha Vantage outage and the absence of any live NQ price structure to assess.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Tail holds at 2% (low) as NQ remains in the CME weekend halt with no live price-path evidence available to assess for failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure. Stress eases slightly to 9% (low) continuing the halt's natural decay toward the weekend floor as no session is repricing; the standing Strait of Hormuz crisis remains a contained background driver rather than an actively repricing one. Confidence eases to 36% (low), reflecting the continued Alpha Vantage rate-limit outage and one additional hour with no live NQ price action to evaluate, offset by clean WebSearch corroboration that nothing material changed since the prior run. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active regardless of the current EA_ON state. The next evidence-relevant checkpoint remains CME's Sunday reopen (~22:00-23:00 UTC / 00:00-01:00 CEST Monday), where any weekend Hormuz headline could produce a gap; a Tail upgrade would require an observed failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction in NQ itself at or after that reopen, not the standing headline risk alone.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (6-13%) through most of the trailing 24 hours, easing from Thursday evening's post-CPI/PPI digestion through Friday's Asian/European session into a stable single-digit floor, holding 7-9% through Friday's confirmed UMich/Retail Sales misses and the Broadcom/Applied Materials semis drag, easing further as AMD's prior ambiguity resolved higher into the Friday close, and finally to 2% over the last two hours as NQ entered the CME weekend halt with no live price-path evidence to evaluate. Stress ran from the low-30s Thursday evening down into the mid-20s in the early Friday Asian session, rebuilt through the European morning and the confirmed UMich print (peaking near 44%), held roughly 40-41% through the U.S. afternoon, eased through the cash close, and fell further to single digits over the last two hours as the weekend halt began and today's semis-earnings dispersion stopped actively repricing. The standing Strait of Hormuz crisis provided a persistent, contained event-importance driver throughout. No published assessment exists for the 20:00 UTC hour (a run did not publish in that window).
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to hold at the low weekend floor (2%) through the entire 24-hour horizon as NQ futures remain in the CME weekend halt with no live session to evaluate; the horizon ends at 22:00 UTC Saturday, still well ahead of CME's scheduled Sunday reopen (~22:00-23:00 UTC), which sits just beyond this window. Stress is projected to settle at the low weekend floor (~7%) from the second hour onward, held there by the absence of any active session rather than a resolved risk picture -- the standing Strait of Hormuz crisis remains the principal source of weekend headline/gap risk into Sunday's reopen. No forecast slot currently implies an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to decay gradually from the mid-30s toward the low-20s as the horizon moves further from this run's live evidence and further from any live trading session.
